lanes.mission: Build the research method for FIELD LAB itself: derive falsifiable hypotheses, controls, instrumentation and tiny implementation probes for whether cross-mode projections improve agency/comprehension/memory/delight rather than merely novelty.
required_design: For every claim: OBJECT → MANIPULATION → CONTROL → OBSERVABLE → FAIL CONDITION → RETURN.
Use a boring/minimal baseline against every spectacular treatment.
Separate source evidence from encounter profile from human interpretation.
Prefer within-source A/B or counterbalanced trials over anecdotes.
Use the existing EXCITEMENT event vector as a provisional lens, never a scalar score.
first_experiments: PULSE: metronome baseline vs 3:2/4:3/5:4 field; measure tap phase error, retention after short delay, and subjective legibility.
READ: ordinary paced RSVP/reading baseline vs ghost-race + explicit regression; measure comprehension/recall, regressions, completion time and perceived agency.
LOCI: linear token list baseline vs addressed path; measure ordered recall and source-position recovery.
INK: plain line rendering baseline vs wet diffusion + speed-sensitive deposit; measure whether users can intentionally reproduce target stroke qualities, not whether it merely looks beautiful.
RIDE: constant spectacle baseline vs rare anticipated consequential events; measure which events are noticed, anticipated and remembered and whether users can state the source cause.
CROSS-MODE: one exact addressed source passes through two projections; verify identity/address survive and test whether the second projection adds retained value.
lanes.implementation_boundary: Small local fixtures, deterministic probes and exportable result packets are allowed. No new app, universal research dashboard, scoring ontology or promoted shared core.
lanes.output: One ranked experiment packet with the smallest runnable study first, instrumentation schema, baseline, pass/fail gates, and any bounded patch proposal.
